samples.text:
The plans show the ground floor of a public library now and how it will look after a proposed redesign. Overall, some parts will stay the same, but many areas will be smaller and some new rooms like a café and a computer room will be added.

At present, when people come in from the entrance in the south, the reception and returns desk is in front of them and the newspapers and magazines section is behind it. The fiction books is on the left side and non-fiction is on the right. In the north there are a big reference and reading room, the children's books, and also an office and toilets in the north-east.

In the new design, the reception, office and toilets will not change. The fiction and non-fiction sections will be smaller, because a café will be added next to fiction and a computer room next to non-fiction. The newspapers area will be replaced with self-service machines. Also, the reference room will be divide into a quiet study and meeting rooms, and the children's area will have a story corner.
samples.why: Overview present but general · main proposed changes covered · linking mostly basic · adequate vocabulary with left and right used instead of compass directions · several agreement and verb form errors.

samples.text:
The plans compare the current layout of a public library's ground floor with a proposed redesign. Overall, the new design would reduce the space used for traditional book collections and introduce more areas for technology, study and social activities, while the reception, office and toilets would remain where they are.

In the southern half of the building, the reception and returns desk just inside the entrance would stay the same, but the newspapers and magazines area behind it would be replaced by self-service machines. The fiction section in the south-west and the non-fiction section in the south-east would both lose a large part of their space, making room for a café to the north of fiction and a computer room to the north of non-fiction.

In the northern half, the large reference and reading room in the north-west would be split into two parts, with a quiet study area on the western side and meeting rooms next to it. The children's books section would become a children's area with a story corner, although it would occupy the same space as before. The office and the toilets in the north-east would be unchanged.
samples.why: Clear overview of the direction of change · logical division into southern and northern areas · effective cohesion · appropriate vocabulary with conditional forms used consistently · few, if any, errors.

samples.text:
The floor plans show the existing ground floor of a public library alongside a proposed redesign. The proposal represents a clear shift away from traditional reading space towards technology and flexible study areas, with the entrance, reception, office and toilets left as they are.

Visitors entering from the south would still find the reception and returns desk immediately ahead of them. Beyond it, however, the newspapers and magazines section would give way to self-service machines. On either side, the fiction and non-fiction collections, which currently fill the south-western and south-eastern corners, would each lose a substantial part of their present depth; the space released would accommodate a café on the western side and a computer room on the eastern side.

The northern half of the floor would also be reorganised. The spacious reference and reading room in the north-west would be subdivided into a quiet study area and a set of meeting rooms, whereas the children's books section would be reinvented as a children's area with a story corner, occupying the same floor space. The office and toilets in the north-eastern corner would remain unaltered.
samples.why: Insightful overview · proposed changes skilfully sequenced as a visitor moves through the building · sophisticated cohesion · precise vocabulary (subdivided, space released) · wide range of structures, accurate throughout.
